summary:
Snapshot for Oct 13, 2026, GLP-1 focus only. The plague topics from earlier snapshots are dropped. Two stories lead.

1. **Bootleg "Reta".** CBS News reported on Oct 13 that the FDA received reports of two deaths after people took products sold as retatrutide. Whether the product caused the deaths is unconfirmed, and nobody knows what was actually in the vials. NewsNation, Becker's and MedPage Today picked it up the same day, and Australia's Google Trends shows "retatrutide" as a daily trending search. This fits our proven myth-bust format about online and unapproved products (55 views; the plague "cures online" version got 82).
2. **Retatrutide's TRIUMPH-2 trial in The Lancet.** It tested adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight. At the top dose, weight fell 18.8% vs 5.1% on placebo at 80 weeks (treatment-regimen estimand). Lilly reports earnings on Oct 29, which will keep retatrutide in the news. This fits the "Did [new drug] beat tirzepatide?" format behind our long-form breakout.

Other rising topics:
- **GLP-1s and biological aging.** CNN covered it on Oct 13, and syndication is spreading. We need a careful "does it slow aging?" angle. We already ran a carousel on this, so make it a Short.
- **GLP-1s and nail changes.** A survey study presented at the EADV dermatology congress (self-reported, half had nail problems before treatment) reached ScienceDaily and VICE. It suits our "what does it do to my body?" format.

Evergreen topics with fresh hooks:
- Orforglipron (Foundayo, approved Apr 1, 2026) works across menopause stages
- Protecting muscle on tirzepatide, with an early animal-study hook (iBio's IBIO-610)
- GLP-1 nausea vs indigestion (Medscape)
- Telling your surgical team you take a GLP-1, with a new systematic review on cardiac surgery
- Wegovy pill vs shot uptake
- Sleep apnea and heart failure
- An observational study linking GLP-1 use to lower death risk in older adults with fatty liver disease

Lower-priority caution picks:
- Korea's vision-loss reports (safety scares have underperformed for us)
- The Zepbound + Taltz psoriasis trial (momentum is fading)

Rejected:
- Advertorials for cheap compounded or telehealth GLP-1 plans
- Price indexes of online compounded products

What I checked: the CBS report, TRIUMPH-2 figures (Lancet/HCPLive), the CNN aging piece, the EADV nail data, the Age and Ageing fatty-liver cohort, orforglipron's approval status and the weight-regain pilot trial. The pilot (10.75% regain over 4 months) was already used in our Oct 13 Short, so I didn't list it again.

candidates.topic: Bootleg 'Reta': two deaths reported to the FDA after people took products sold as retatrutide (CBS News investigation, Oct 13). Retatrutide is unapproved as of Oct 2026, and nobody knows what the vials actually contained
candidates.angle: Myth-bust: 'Online Reta isn't the trial drug.' Retatrutide is still investigational (as of Oct 2026). CBS reported two death reports to the FDA, but it hasn't been confirmed that the product caused them. Products bought online may not contain what the label says. What the real trials tested, under medical supervision. Close by pointing to a prescriber. Never name a seller or explain how to buy.
candidates.why_now: CBS broke the story on Oct 13. NewsNation, Becker's and MedPage Today followed the same day, and 'retatrutide' is a Google Trends daily search in Australia. Most creators haven't covered it yet, and it fits our proven myth-bust format about online products (55 views).

evidence.signal: The FDA received reports of two deaths (July: a 41-year-old with cardiac arrest; September: a 49-year-old with dehydration, malnutrition and cardiac arrest) after people took products claiming to be retatrutide. It isn't clear the drug was to blame.
Follow-up report on the deaths after people took products claiming to be Lilly's retatrutide
Picked up the black-market retatrutide death reports
'retatrutide' trending at 500+ searches

candidates.topic: Retatrutide in type 2 diabetes (TRIUMPH-2, The Lancet): at the top dose (12 mg), 18.8% average weight loss vs 5.1% on placebo at 80 weeks (treatment-regimen estimand), in adults with T2D and obesity or overweight
candidates.angle: 'Did retatrutide beat tirzepatide in type 2 diabetes?' Give the one number with its population and estimand. Be clear that it was tested against placebo, not head to head with tirzepatide. Explain the triple hormone action simply. It is investigational as of Oct 2026. Close with the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: The Lancet paper is out, Medical Xpress covered it on Oct 13, Motley Fool and Yahoo have Q3 earnings pieces, and the bootleg-Reta story is pushing search interest. It suits our long-form breakout format ('Did X beat tirzepatide?').

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-2: randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in adults with obesity and T2D
Weight down up to 18.8% in adults with T2D and obesity
Treatment-regimen estimand: -11.9%, -16.8% and -18.8% (4, 9 and 12 mg) vs -5.1% on placebo at 80 weeks; A1C reductions of 1.7%, 2.0% and 1.9% vs 0.8%
'Triple-action drug retatrutide delivers major weight loss for people with diabetes' (Oct 13)

candidates.topic: Do GLP-1 medicines slow biological aging? CNN (Oct 13): in drugmaker-reported data, people on the drugs had biological-age readings about 2–3 years lower than on placebo. It's unclear whether that comes from the weight loss itself
candidates.angle: 'Does Mounjaro or Ozempic slow aging?' Answer within 10 s: early aging-clock data, reported by the drugmakers, not a lifespan result. Explain what an aging clock measures and what is proven (heart, kidney and liver benefits in specific trial populations). Experts say it's too early to take these drugs to live longer. Never use #antiaging.
candidates.why_now: CNN ran it on Oct 13 and it's spreading through syndication (KVUE, NewsNation, KRDO), following MIT Technology Review on Oct 6. Our Oct 13 carousel on this can't reach anyone (carousels reach 0–3 accounts), so redo it as a Short.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 drugs appear to slow aging processes; about 2–3 years lower biological age vs placebo; unclear if this comes from weight loss; too early to use them for longevity
'Weight-loss drugs show signs of slowing biological aging, say drugmakers' (company-reported aging-clock data)
'GLP-1 weight-loss drugs slow biological aging, recent studies show'

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and nail changes: in a survey presented at EADV 2026, 39% of users reported nail detachment vs 9% of non-users with T2D or obesity. The data was self-reported, about half had nail problems before treatment, and the cause isn't established
candidates.angle: 'Can Ozempic or Mounjaro affect your nails?' Plain answer in 10 s: it was a survey, the cause isn't proven, and researchers think fast weight loss and eating less may play a part. A helpful, non-scary 'you' action: keep protein up, and tell your prescriber or a dermatologist if your nails change. Mention the kidney caveat with the protein tip.
candidates.why_now: Presented at EADV in early October, it has now spread to ScienceDaily (Oct 12) and VICE (Oct 13, 'new GLP-1 side effect'). It fits our 'what does it do to my body?' format, which is our best GLP-1 pattern. Keep the tone calm to avoid the safety-scare drop.

evidence.signal: 1,904 people in 4 countries; 39% vs 9% nail detachment; about half of users had nail problems before treatment; possibly an indirect effect of weight loss
GLP-1 users report more nail detachment and hair loss than non-users
'Popular weight loss drugs linked to a surprising fingernail problem' (Oct 12)

candidates.topic: Does menopause stage change results on orforglipron (Foundayo)? A new ATTAIN-1 analysis found weight loss in pre-, peri- and postmenopausal women alike over 72 weeks
candidates.angle: 'Does menopause stop GLP-1 pills from working?' Encouraging answer, kept within the analysis's scope (roughly 142–225 women per group, 72 weeks, vs placebo). Orforglipron is FDA-approved for chronic weight management (Apr 1, 2026). Explain how it differs from the Wegovy pill (no food or water timing rules). Close with the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: Medical News Today and Healthline covered it on Oct 13. Menopause plus GLP-1 is a big search intent for our 25–65 audience, and few creators cover the drug by name.

evidence.signal: Orforglipron (Foundayo) produced weight loss regardless of menopausal stage
'Weight loss with Orforglipron: Does menopausal stage matter?' (Oct 13)
Foundayo approval history: FDA-approved Apr 1, 2026

candidates.topic: How to protect muscle on tirzepatide (Mounjaro): SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy plus protein and strength training. Hook: iBio's IBIO-610 shifted semaglutide weight loss toward fat in an 8-week primate study
candidates.angle: 'Tirzepatide: are you losing fat or muscle?' Start with the 160-person body-scan substudy, then the recommended habits. Label them 'recommended', not 'shown to protect muscle on tirzepatide'. Include the protein kidney caveat and start exercise gently. The IBIO-610 work is only an animal-study teaser ('early, in monkeys, not tested in people').
keywords: how to keep muscle on ozempic
candidates.why_now: This is the playbook's top double-down topic and our best cross-platform GLP-1 post (98 YouTube views, 61 reach on Instagram). The iBio primate data released Oct 13 gives a fresh hook, and it also fills the carousel-to-Short conversion slot.

evidence.signal: IBIO-610 shifted semaglutide weight loss toward fat in obese primates (preclinical, company-reported)
GLP-1 use and frailty and falls in adults with T2D (Oct 7), relevant to the muscle angle

candidates.topic: Feeling awful on your GLP-1? How doctors tell functional dyspepsia (ongoing indigestion) from GLP-1 stomach side effects, plus habits that can make nausea easier
candidates.angle: A practical 'you' Short: common stomach side effects and the habits that can help (smaller meals, stopping when full, lower-fat meals, fluids unless you've been told to limit them). Give the red flags that need a prescriber call quickly (severe or ongoing belly pain, vomiting). This also converts the planned 'nausea and constipation' carousel into a Short.
keywords: how to stop nausea on wegovy
candidates.why_now: Medscape (Oct 13) and Yahoo Creators (Oct 11) have fresh pieces on it, and it's the playbook's first carousel-to-Short conversion. Practical 'you' actions are a proven signal (the anesthesia Short got 82).

evidence.signal: 'Functional Dyspepsia or GLP-1 Adverse Effect? How to Tell' (Oct 13)
'Feeling awful on your GLP-1? The drug may not be what's making you miserable' (Oct 11)

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill vs Wegovy shot: oral semaglutide topped 100,000 obesity prescriptions a month within 2 months, and the JAMA Netw Open paper on early US uptake
candidates.angle: 'Wegovy pill vs shot: what's actually different?' Cover how you take each one (the pill has morning empty-stomach rules), results in their own trials (not head to head), and who's starting it (Novo reports most new users are new to GLP-1). The pill was approved Dec 22, 2025. Close with the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: This is its third snapshot (momentum 70→73). Medscape's Oct 12 '100K monthly' piece and The Pharma Letter add fresh hooks, and the Amazon Pharmacy availability story is driving searches.

evidence.signal: Early Adoption and Diffusion of Oral Semaglutide in US Adults With Obesity
'Oral Semaglutide Obesity Rx Tops 100K Monthly in 2 Months' (Oct 12)
Novo reports the Wegovy pill passed 3M US prescriptions; most new users are new to GLP-1

candidates.topic: On a GLP-1 and having surgery? A new systematic review of GLP-1 plus insulin vs insulin alone for blood-sugar control around cardiac surgery in T2D
candidates.angle: A sequel to our 82-view anesthesia Short: 'On semaglutide or tirzepatide? Tell your surgical team.' Use the new review as a hook about blood-sugar control around surgery in adults with T2D. The action is to tell your anesthesia team and prescriber before any procedure. No stopping or timing advice.
candidates.why_now: The review was published Oct 12, and the format is proven: the surgery/anesthesia Short is our #3 GLP-1 post.

evidence.signal: Systematic review: GLP-1 RAs plus insulin vs insulin for perioperative glycemic control in T2D cardiac surgery (Oct 12)

candidates.topic: GLP-1 use linked to 45% lower death risk and 28% lower risk of liver decompensation in adults 65+ with fatty liver disease (MASLD). Observational TriNetX cohort of 87,860, published in Age and Ageing
candidates.angle: 'Fatty liver after 65: what GLP-1 users' records show.' Use 'linked to', not 'cuts'. Keep the population exact. Report the flip side too: the GLP-1 group had more osteoporosis and retinopathy diagnoses and no lower heart attack or stroke risk. Researchers say randomized trials in older adults are needed. Close with the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: Medical Xpress covered it on Oct 13 and few creators have it yet. It fits the 'benefits beyond weight' pillar, and FDA approval of Wegovy for MASH gives it search interest.

evidence.signal: 87,860 adults 65+ with MASLD; 45% lower all-cause death and 28% lower decompensation; more osteoporosis and retinopathy; no MI or stroke reduction; not causal
Protocol for a meta-analysis of RCTs of GLP-1 RAs in MASH

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and alcohol: a Lancet 2026 RCT found fewer heavy-drinking days in adults with alcohol use disorder and obesity, and a major new trial will test semaglutide in alcohol and opioid use disorder
candidates.angle: 'Does Ozempic reduce alcohol cravings? What the trial found.' Say who was studied (108 adults with AUD and obesity, 26 weeks) and that semaglutide is not approved for alcohol or opioid use disorder. Explain the brain's reward system. Point to real support resources and the prescriber.
candidates.why_now: News-Medical (Oct 13) reported the new AUD/OUD trial, and Medical Economics (Oct 11) ran 'semaglutide cuts heavy drinking'. It's part of our 'promising early research' pillar.

evidence.signal: 'Major trial seeks to test semaglutide on adults with alcohol and opioid use disorder' (Oct 13)

evidence.source: GPnotebook (summary of Klausen et al., Lancet 2026)
evidence.signal: 108 adults with AUD and obesity; semaglutide reduced heavy-drinking days and craving vs placebo over 26 weeks

candidates.topic: Is tirzepatide (Zepbound) approved for sleep apnea? FDA approval for moderate-to-severe OSA with obesity, SURMOUNT-OSA, plus a new meta-analysis of GLP-1 RCTs
candidates.angle: Instagram plain-question format: 'Is Zepbound approved for sleep apnea? What FDA says.' Answer in 5 s, give the approved population, and cover what the trial measured (breathing interruptions per hour) and what the meta-analysis adds. Close with the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 2 previous snapshots, there's a new Sleep Breath meta-analysis (Oct 6), and Google News shows the 'zepbound sleep apnea' search still resurfacing. It matches the playbook's Instagram suggestion.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 RAs for obstructive sleep apnea: meta-analysis of RCTs
'fda approves weight-loss drug zepbound for obstructive sleep apnea' resurfacing Oct 13

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) in obesity: Cedars-Sinai study plus a new tirzepatide meta-analysis on heart biomarkers and exercise capacity
candidates.angle: 'Can tirzepatide or semaglutide help a stiff heart?' Explain HFpEF simply, say which trials and populations the evidence comes from, and use 'linked to' for the observational work. Close with the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: Cedars-Sinai published a release on Oct 13, a JCEM tirzepatide meta-analysis came out Oct 13, and Medical Dialogues covered semaglutide in HFpEF. It's part of the 'benefits beyond weight' pillar.

evidence.signal: 'Study: Weight-Loss Drugs May Protect Against Heart Failure' (Oct 13)
Tirzepatide in heart failure: cardiorenal biomarkers and functional capacity, systematic review and meta-analysis

candidates.topic: Safiglipron, a new oral small-molecule GLP-1 pill, vs dapagliflozin in type 2 diabetes: phase 3 RCT in Nature Medicine
candidates.angle: 'Another GLP-1 pill is coming: what safiglipron's phase 3 showed.' Name both sides of the comparison (vs dapagliflozin, in T2D). It is investigational as of Oct 2026. Place it next to orforglipron and the Wegovy pill.
candidates.why_now: It's a fresh Nature Medicine phase 3 paper (Oct 5) with almost no consumer coverage. But brand-new compounds underperform for us (emerging GLP-1 median is 32), so treat it as a secondary pick.

evidence.signal: Safiglipron vs dapagliflozin in T2D: randomized, double-blind, active-comparator phase 3

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide plus ixekizumab (Zepbound + Taltz) for psoriasis with obesity: in TOGETHER-PsO, 40.6% reached completely clear skin vs 29.0% on ixekizumab alone (Lilly-reported)
candidates.angle: 'Can Zepbound help psoriasis treatment work better?' Credit the figures to Lilly, keep the population exact (psoriasis plus obesity) and the comparator (ixekizumab alone). Explain the inflammation link simply. Close with the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: This is its third snapshot, but momentum is easing (62→60). Yahoo Finance and The Hill coverage keeps it alive. It's a niche audience.

evidence.signal: 'Lilly's Zepbound enhances Taltz efficacy in psoriasis study'

candidates.topic: South Korea's drug agency lists vision loss (NAION) as a rare side effect of Wegovy and Mounjaro; first suspected Korean case reported
candidates.angle: Only as a calm 'what we know' explainer: NAION is very rare (EMA PRAC said 'very rare' for semaglutide in 2025). Name the sign that needs urgent care (sudden painless vision loss in one eye) and tell people to talk to their prescriber. Never fear-bait.
candidates.why_now: Several Korean outlets ran it on Oct 13, and US lawsuit coverage keeps it alive. But our own NAION Short got 32 views, below the median, and safety scares underperform. Low priority.

evidence.signal: 'South Korea reports 1st suspected vision-loss case linked to GLP-1 drugs' (Oct 13)
PRAC assessed NAION as a possible very rare side effect of semaglutide

candidates.topic: $86–$99/month compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide telehealth plans and online 'price indexes' (press releases and advertorials)
candidates.angle: Not for content. Promoting or comparing compounded or online sources breaks a channel guardrail. Only the general bootleg-Reta warning above is allowed.
candidates.why_now: Multiple press releases on Oct 12; excluded under the guardrails.
